title: Affix-aware cache key canonicalization and TTL gradient controller with canary safety gates
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a safe, measurable way to improve KV/prefix cache hit rate by changing cache key normalization and TTL allocation. This ticket implements an affix-aware canonicalizer that preserves meaningful suffixes/prefixes for model requests (eg. user scoped tokens, conversation suffixes), introduces a TTL gradient controller that sets TTLs as a continuous knob tied to estimated marginal hit-value, and builds a canary + safety gate rollout automation for config apply/rollback. Goal: reduce per-token cost while keeping tail latency and output quality stable.
background: Previous work focused on prefix popularity simulators and TTL autotuners (see dependencies). We observed that naive canonicalization collapsed high-value suffix information and amplified cache pollution. A single TTL per prefix can't capture the long-tail affinity patterns in conversation state. We will instead canonicalize with affix awareness and use a marginal-hit-value model to allocate TTLs along a gradient, then roll changes with staged canaries tied to real cost metrics and quality checks.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Primary: net reduction in hosted token cost per 10k requests by >= 6% during steady-state canary. Secondary: no regression in 99th percentile token latency (>5% relative), conversational accuracy regressions on a 5k prompt eval set <0.5% absolute, and cache hit improvement on monitored prefixes >= 12% in top 10k prefixes. Safety: any single canary segment with >=3% cost uplift or >=0.3% accuracy regression must trigger automatic rollback.
approach_summary: 1) Build "affix-preserving" canonicalization library that tags suffix/prefix segments and applies suffix-safe hashing. 2) Implement a TTL Gradient Controller service that computes per-prefix TTLs using a marginal-hit-value model (uses recent hit/miss traces + Holt-Winters smoothing for decay). 3) Create canary plan: local simulator -> shadow traffic -> 1% traffic canary -> automated metric gate evaluation -> progressive 1/5/20/100% rollout. 4) Add automated rollback runbook and Kubernetes operator for safe config apply and rapid revert.
design_decisions:
- Canonicalization will not strip terminal tokens shorter than 6 chars to preserve message-level cues.
- We use a two-tier hashing: namespace hash + affix-stable suffix hash to avoid cross-namespace collisions.
- TTLs are a continuous value (seconds) bounded [30, 86400] and smoothed via EWMA before apply.
- Cost model uses per-prefix marginal saved compute tokens computed from historical samples rather than static popularity buckets.
- Rollout uses metric-driven gates implemented in the rollout controller (cost, latency, accuracy).
implementation_plan: Phase A (1 week): canonicalization library + unit tests and static analysis; create synthetic dataset for affix patterns. Phase B (2 weeks): TTL Gradient Controller prototype, offline scoring, and backtest against 30 days of traces (shadow mode). Phase C (1.5 weeks): rollout automation, canary wiring, monitoring dashboards and alerting. Phase D (0.5 weeks): small production canary and staged expansion with automated rollback. Work will land across runtime, router, and console repos.
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-prefix hit-rate, effective TTL distribution, per-segment cost delta, 99p latency, eval-set accuracy. Alerts: automatic rollback if cost delta > +3% in a segment, accuracy drop >0.3% absolute on eval queries, or 99p latency > baseline * 1.05 for 5m. Add tracing hooks to correlate cache hits with request traces for debugging.
experiment_plan:
- Offline: backtest TTL gradient assignments using last 30 days of request traces and the shadow cache simulator to compute projected cost savings and hit uplift.
- Shadow run: deploy canonicalizer + TTL controller in shadow for 48 hours to measure divergence.
- Canary run: progressive traffic percentages [1,5,20,100] with 12-24h holds at each stage and automatic gating.
- Eval set: 5k curated prompts (edge cases + high-value prefixes) run continuously against canary and baseline to detect semantic regressions.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback operator will revert the applied TTL and canonicalization config if any metric gate trips. Manual rollback steps documented: 1) Pause rollout via console. 2) Revert to last-known-good config via K8s secrets rollback. 3) Notify customers via incident channel if impact > medium. Postmortem responsibilities assigned to assignee and on-call runtime engineer.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer (affix cases), property-based tests for hashing stability, integration tests for router TTL application, load tests to validate latency under synthetic high-hit scenarios, and a functional eval-run comparing outputs between baseline and canary on eval-set.
open_questions: 1) Do we allow user-configurable affix rules per tenant or keep global? 2) How to account for dynamic prompt templating that injects volatile IDs? 3) Should TTL controller incorporate cost-per-token forecasts for upcoming model changes?
